criteria.name: The card's title.
criteria.role: Region (a named section), its title a heading.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the title, body and links grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the card's content stack in one column, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <section> element.
The card is named by its title in aria-label.
I SEE its body as a paragraph.
WHEN I move into the card with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its title, the role of region, and its title again as a heading at its level.
WHEN I Tab to a link in the card I HEAR the link's own name, clear without the card around it.

criteria.semantics: Expanded, as on html: a group of its heading, its body as text and its links as a list. Once GPUI exposes a tree: those core kinds' nodes, an AccessKit Group named by the title around them.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the card by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.
Moves through the card's links in reading order.

criteria.name: The card's title.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the title, body and links grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the title, body and links drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the title, body and links at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the title, body and links drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the title, body and links whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A card adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the title as a heading over the body.
WHEN I move into the card with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its title as a group and as a heading at its level.

announce.api: AXGroup named by the title, then an AXHeading (AccessKit Role::Group, Heading).
announce.says: "Field notes, group", then "Field notes, heading level 3".

announce.api: ControlType Group named by the title, then a Text with its HeadingLevel.
ATSPI_ROLE_PANEL named by the title, then ATSPI_ROLE_HEADING.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
